title: Who Gets In and Why: A Year Inside College Admissions
description: From award-winning higher education journalist and New York Times bestselling author Jeffrey Selingo comes a revealing look from inside the admissions office—one that identifies surprising strategies that will aid in the college search. Getting into a top-ranked college has never seemed more impossible, with acceptance rates at some elite universities dipping into the single digits. In Who Gets In and Why , journalist and higher education expert Jeffrey Selingo dispels entrenched notions of how to compete and win at the admissions game, and reveals that teenagers and parents have much to gain by broadening their notion of what qualifies as a “good college.” Hint: it’s not all about the sticker on the car window. Selingo, who was embedded in three different admissions offices—a selective private university, a leading liberal arts college, and a flagship public campus—closely observed gatekeepers as they made their often agonizing and sometimes life-changing decisions. He also followed select students and their parents, and he traveled around the country meeting with high school counselors, marketers, behind-the-scenes consultants, and college rankers. While many have long believed that admissions is merit-based, rewarding the best students, Who Gets In and Why presents a more complicated truth, showing that “who gets in” is frequently more about the college’s agenda than the applicant. In a world where thousands of equally qualified students vie for a fixed number of spots at elite institutions, admissions officers often make split-second decisions based on a variety of factors—like diversity, money, and, ultimately, whether a student will enroll if accepted. title: Inside Elite College Admissions: 10 Real-World Case Studies
description: Strong grades. Impressive activities. So what makes an application memorable? See how ten students brought their interests, choices, and experiences together in applications that earned places at some of the world’s most selective universities. In Inside Elite College Admissions: 10 Real-World Case Studies , experienced college counselors Caroline Linger and Jose Kumar take you beyond acceptance announcements and achievement lists to explore the individual journeys behind them. Through detailed, anonymized profiles of students admitted to Harvard, Princeton, Yale, Stanford, Cornell, Brown, the University of Chicago, Johns Hopkins, and Duke, discover how students developed their interests, pursued meaningful projects, and communicated what mattered to them. From connecting music with scientific research to using theater for global advocacy, these stories show how curiosity becomes action, and how action gives an application depth. Inside, you’ll discover: 10 distinct student journeys with practical lessons you can apply to your own planning. 25 real-world project ideas to help you explore your interests and create meaningful work. Ways to connect academic interests, extracurricular activities, and personal experiences into a compelling narrative. How authenticity, purpose, and resilience can strengthen the story an application tells. Drawing on decades of counseling experience, Caroline and Jose help students and families approach admissions with greater clarity, creativity, and direction. Whether you’re beginning high school or preparing your applications, this book will help you think more deeply about what you pursue, why it matters, and how to communicate it. Your strongest application begins long before you fill in the form. It begins with what you choose to do next

title: College Admission: From Application to Acceptance, Step by Step
description: College Admission is the ultimate user's manual and go-to guide for any student or family approaching the college application process. Featuring the wise counsel of more than 50 deans of admission, no other guide has such thorough, expert, compassionate, and professional advice. Let’s be honest: applying to college can be stressful for students and parents. But here’s the good news: you can get in. Robin Mamlet has been dean of admission at three of America's most selective colleges, and journalist and parent Christine VanDeVelde has been through the process first hand. With this book, you will feel like you have both a dean of admission and a parent who has been there at your side. title: THE FOUR PILLARS OF COLLEGE ADMISSIONS: REPLACE WORRY WITH A SYSTEM
description: What if getting into college wasn't the hardest part? Every year, millions of families enter the college admissions process overwhelmed by deadlines, financial aid forms, essays, rankings, test scores, and endless advice. The result is often stress, confusion, and costly mistakes that could have been avoided. In The Four Pillars of College Admissions, educator, Army veteran, coach, and admissions advisor Grigory Agrest offers a different approach: replace worry with a system. Drawing on years of experience helping students, first-generation families, immigrant households, and parents navigate one of the most stressful periods of a teenager's life, Agrest reveals the four pillars that drive successful college admissions: Academics that demonstrate growth and readiness Activities that build meaningful depth instead of résumé padding College knowledge that helps families make informed decisions Personal growth that creates confidence, resilience, and long-term success Inside, you'll learn how to: Build a realistic college list Write authentic essays that stand out Navigate FAFSA, CSS Profile, scholarships, and financial aid Avoid common admissions mistakes Have productive family conversations about money Reduce stress and increase clarity throughout the process Prepare for college success beyond the acceptance letter Whether you're a parent searching for answers at midnight, a student feeling overwhelmed by expectations, or a first-generation family trying to understand how the system works, this book provides the practical roadmap you've been looking for. Stop guessing. Stop panicking. Start building a plan. title: The Truth about College Admission: A Family Guide to Getting In and Staying Together
description: Updated and completely revised, the ultimate family guide to managing a college search in a positive way. Is your family just starting to think about visiting colleges? Maybe you are in the throes of the college search, feeling stressed out and overwhelmed. Miss a deadline? Should you be looking in-state or out-of-state, big school or small? How do you pay for it, and what is a "FAFSA" anyway? The Truth about College Admission is the easy-to-follow, comprehensive, go-to guide for families. Brennan Barnard and Rick Clark—with combined decades of experience and insight from both the high school and university sides of the process—provide critical advice, thoughtful strategies, helpful direction, and invaluable reassurance during the long and often bewildering college admission journey. This book covers every important step: searching for colleges, creating a list of prospective schools, weighing financial considerations, crafting an application, learning what schools are looking for academically and outside the classroom, and understanding how colleges decide whom to accept. Helpful sections like "Try This," "Talk About This," and "Check In," and "Extra Credit" show your family how to have open and balanced conversations to keep everyone on the same page, feeling less stressed, and actually enjoying the adventure together. This completely revised second edition includes new information on affordability and aid that addresses important financial considerations. It also explores changes in standardized testing and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.
